column3: The corner method (docs/engines/ranges.md): likely is the plan as entered, the number every screen shows. Then the whole plan is run again with each uncertain input at its low and at its high, the rest as entered. An input's swing on an output is the gap between its two runs; the swings combine as the root of the sum of their squares, one side at a time (inputs taken as independent). The gut number and the Budget lines are one input (they move together); each income, balance, value and APR is its own. How far an input moves comes from its level and kind (Assumptions: RangeBalance*, RangeSpend*, RangeIncome*, RangeVariable*, RangeApr*, RoughBalanceShare, AprGuessSwing); a typical amount not answered yet moves TypicalLow to TypicalHigh. Outputs: the FI date, the debt-free date, emergency fund months, the monthly surplus, net worth (low, likely, high each) and the FOO step (the earliest and latest step any one input reaches). A date that never comes at an end is blank there (or later). column2: Social Security a month once claimed, today's dollars
column3: Batch 56 (js/math/socialsecurity.js), read by the projection (M9P). Each person's benefit at full retirement age (the PIA): the number off their my Social Security statement with its level (Gut, Estimate, Know it; Gut moves it 20% either way, Estimate 5%), else an estimate: today's gross pay every year from 22 to the stop age (the same share of the national average wage), capped at the wage base, the best 35 years averaged into AIME, then 90% up to $1,286, 32% to $7,749 and 15% above (2026 bend points, SSA); always a Gut range (AIME 20% either way). Full retirement age by birth year (SS_fra: 67 from 1960). Claim age 62 to 70: 5/9 of 1% a month off for the first 36 months early and 5/12 of 1% beyond; 8% a year added past full retirement age. Spousal: half the partner's PIA less your own, from the later of the two claims, 25/36 of 1% a month off for the first 36 months early and 5/12 of 1% beyond, nothing for waiting. Survivor: from the month one reaches Plan to age, the other keeps the larger of their own and the benefit the partner was getting (at least 82.5% of the partner's PIA if they claimed early). Trust fund switch: 83% from January 2034 (2026 Trustees Report). Today's dollars: the COLA only keeps pace with prices, so a benefit is flat in real terms.

column2: The quick calculators: a HYSA switch, lump sum or a little each month, a warranty, cost per use, Return on Hassle, worth it, personal inflation, starting earlier, cut it or invest it (the round $30k / $90k rule), debt consolidation, unemployment and runway, leaving a job, kids, a pet, a first apartment, roommates, the W-4 check, the month at a glance
column3: Run of Nov 25 2026 (Not built, groups 1 to 5), Part 2 (js/math/quick.js, copied to game/core/quick.js; js/math/quickplan.js). One small page each, drawn by js/solo/calc.js. HYSA: balance and a monthly amount grown at each rate, compounded monthly; the gap in a year and over 5 years. Lump sum or spread: all of it at the return now, against a 1/n piece each month with the rest earning the cash rate; the gap is the expected cost of spreading. Warranty: chance x repair cost next to the price; the chance where they meet = price / repair. Cost per use = (price - resale) / uses. Return on Hassle = dollars saved / hours, next to what an hour of work pays. Worth it = cost per use and price / hourly pay, before or after. Personal inflation = sum of each part's share of spending x its price change. Starting earlier: the same monthly amount from two ages to 65 at the plan's real return; catch-up = monthly x FV(early) / FV(late). Consolidation: payoff months and interest now (M31, M32) against one loan of balance / (1 - fee) at its rate and years. NY unemployment: high quarter / 26 (over $3,575; at least $143), else / 25, at most the weekly maximum, for 26 weeks; runway with the benefit in for its weeks. Leaving a job: cash / (spending + health cover - business profit after federal and self-employment tax, M12); the profit that covers it all = M13. Kids, pet, apartment: the person's own amounts added up by age, by year, or to get the keys. Roommates: the household split engine (M9N) by room size (percent of the space), by income or equally. W-4: federal tax (M10) less the child tax credit, against withheld so far + each paycheck left; short: Step 4(c) = owed / paychecks left; over: Step 4(b) = refund x paychecks a year / (paychecks left x top rate). Month at a glance: M27 and M28. Added Nov 26 2026 (Eli's answer to QUESTIONS 608 a): cut it or invest it. kept = the amount x 12 x the years; invested = the same amount a month at the yearly return after inflation, compounded monthly (qcInvested, the one growth line starting earlier also uses); ratio = invested / kept. The headline is round on purpose: at 30 years and 7% it is Eli's rule scaled by the amount ($30k and $90k for $100 a month, cutting is about 1/3 of investing), at any other tap the worked figure to two figures; the exact figures ($36,000 and about $117,000 for $100) are in Show the math. With a plan behind the page, the days on its own FI date (M53 through fiMoveOf).

column2: Gig and self-employed: the price floor, the tax set-aside, retirement for the self-employed and which account first, invoices and late payments, apps and tips added up, a Profit First split
column3: Run of Nov 25 2026 (Not built, groups 1 to 5), Part 5 (js/math/gig.js, copied to game/core/gigcore.js; js/math/gigplan.js on the tax engine). Floor: need = life a month x 12 + health a month x 12 + retirement a year; profit = the self-employed gross that leaves the need after tax (M13, with NY and NYC where set); paid hours = hours a week x the billable share x (52 - weeks off); floor an hour = (profit + costs a month x 12) / paid hours; a day = 8 paid hours; a job = its paid hours. The game: profit = need / (1 - the player's set-aside share). Set-aside: the tax the profit adds on top of any job's pay (householdTax, the 1099 row stacked on the W-2 row: income tax, self-employment tax, state and city), over the profit; a quarter = a year / 4 at the Form 1040-ES dates; so far = profit so far x the share - set aside. Retirement: base = profit - half the self-employment tax (M11); the business's part = 20% of the base, pay counted to the 401(a)(17) cap; SEP = that, at most the 415(c) total; Solo 401(k) = the deferral (the 402(g) limit less what was deferred at a job, at most the base) + the business's part, at most the 415(c) total and the base, + the catch-up (50+, or 60 to 63); IRA = its limit + catch-up, at most the base. Which first: the least paperwork that holds what you want (IRA, then SEP, then Solo 401(k)); with no amount, the one that holds most. Invoices: due = sent + terms (or a typed due date); past = today after due, days past = today - due; ages 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+; days to pay = paid - sent; the reminder step by days past (1, 14, 30, 60). Apps: expected = earned - fee; gap = expected - landed; each app's share of all (cash tips in); tips = app tips + cash. Profit First: each share x real revenue; what the shares leave unplaced; the book's sample 5/50/15/30.

column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 13 (js/math/invest.js, copied to game/core/invest.js; invest.html and the game's Investment mix and fees, Invest or pay debt, Roth or traditional by account). Mix: each class = sum of each account's balance x its share of that class, over the balances whose mix is known; stocks = US + international + stock funds + single companies; drift = stocks - target (your own, else the Vanguard Target Retirement glide path: 90% until 25 years before the stop age, then down to 50% at it and 30% seven years after); a line past 5 points. Three-fund check: the share in US stocks, international stocks, broad stock funds and bonds, and what sits outside them. One company: each company's dollars (the employer's across accounts) / all invested; a line past 10% (FINRA). Fees: each fund's value x its expense ratio + each account fee + the advisor fee x the balance; a fund with no fee counts none and is named; a load: $1,000 x the load. Invest or pay debt: $1,000 x ((1 + APR/12)^60 - 1) next to $1,000 x ((1 + return)^5 - 1). Roth or traditional: rate now = federal + state + city marginal; later = the same on the estimated retirement income; traditional leaves yearly x (now - later) more a year to invest (crRothTrad).

A change is money flows over months: pay that stops for the weeks off (weeks x 12 / 52 months), a leave benefit (NY state disability: 50% of the weekly wage up to $170 a week from the second week, 26 weeks; NY Paid Family Leave 2026: 67% up to $1,228.53 a week, 12 weeks), a cost that rises from a month on, one-time costs in the first month. The cash each month = the cash before + income - spending + the flows in that month (a flow counts for the share of the month it covers). Runway = the month the cash goes below 0, with the part of the last month. Tripwires at 3, 2 and 1 months of the basics. Plan B: the same at the DRAFTT level, or a trim. Levels: cash / (level - what still comes in). Days = months x 30.44.

column2: Giving: the giving rate on the base you pick, the target a share comes to (maaser), one gift in hours, days on the FI date and what it would have grown to, bunching two or three years of giving into one, envelopes inside one account, and the maaser credit for giving ahead
column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 16 (js/math/giving.js, copied to game/core/giving.js; giving.html and the game's Giving). Rate = given a month / the base (gross pay, take-home, or take-home less the work costs you name). Target = the base x your share (10% until you tap one). A gift: hours = gift / your real hourly wage; days = the FI date (M53, the game's freeAt) run with and without the gift; grown = gift x (1 + real return)^years, or each month's gift grown to the FI date. Bunching: each year takes the larger of the standard deduction plus up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of cash gifts, or the other itemized deductions plus the gifts above 0.5% of income; federal tax by the 2026 brackets; every year x N next to N years in one. Envelopes: left = put in - used; the bar = left / put in; not labeled = the account - what the envelopes hold. Maaser credit: a running balance of given - due; with giving ahead off, it stops at zero.

column2: Game feel: start at the finish line (work back from what you need once work is optional to a month to put in today), the race against your past self, the bottleneck finder (eight kinds, Is this really it?), and the made-up composite stories
column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 20 (js/math/feel.js, copied to game/core/feel.js; end.html and the game's Start at the finish line, What's in the way, Role model and rival). Finish line: invested at the end = what you need a year / the withdrawal rate (or the total you name); a month to put in = (the total - what you have grown month by month to the year) x i / ((1 + i)^n - 1), i = (1 + real return)^(1/12) - 1; the gap = that - left over a month; at today's pace: the month what you have plus what is left over reaches the total. Past you: pace = the change in net worth over a stretch / its days x 30.4, the last 90 days next to the 90 before. Bottleneck: points from your numbers (nothing left over 3, less than the finish line needs 2, a later date 2, a low score band 2) and your taps (Yes 2, A little 1, No -1, never below 0); the most points is the call, a tie goes to the kind higher on the list; your pick with Is this really it? wins.

column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 18 (js/math/recap.js; Report › One-pager, Session summary, drafted for you, and the Plan report). Before = the key numbers (keyNumbers) in the last snapshot saved before the session started; now = the key numbers today. Each number takeaway = now, and now - before as up or down (net worth, debt on file, monthly surplus, savings rate). Each date takeaway compares calendar months: the snapshot's month + its months count, and this month + today's count; sooner by the difference, or Recalculating with the new month when it is later (debt free M34; the FI date M53, only once the FI date is unlocked). Each change takeaway = the change log since the session started, in the shared view, grouped by kind of row and what was done (added, updated, removed), a row added in the session counted once; a private row counts and its name never shows. Takeaways: the numbers first, then the changes, the biggest first, 10 at most. Next steps = the next moves (M82), then the client's to-dos, each once, 5 at most.

column2: Asking fewer questions: the cost of not knowing in dollars, one ranking of the open questions, and the stopping rule
column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 17 (js/math/askrank.js, copied to game/core/askrank.js; js/math/nextbest.js sorts Ask me next with the same arRank). Your money a year from now = net worth + 12 x (money in a month - money out a month). The cost of not knowing a blank = |that number with the blank at the high end of its range - with it at the low end| (a month's row: 12 x its width; a balance: its width). Score = dollars / seconds (a tap is 1). Rank: higher score first; within 2% the preferred kind (Ask me next: the spending input when Spending is the big deal), then the list order. Stopping rule: walk the ranked blanks and ask while the dollars asked are under AskStopShare (80%) of all the open dollars; the rest move 20% or less and can wait (the 80/20 rule). A question the plan cannot run without is always asked.

column3: Run Finish everything partly built, Part 21 (js/math/canonmath.js, copied to game/core/canonmath.js). F-You money: months = what you could reach without a penalty / (spending - work costs that stop + health cover on your own); on the noodle budget: reach / the noodle month; marks at 3, 6, 12, 24 months. The nine: each SLAM step on the Money Guy's nine (0b and 1 on 1, 5b on 5, 9 on 7). Hand-off: worth = hours a month x your hour; gap = worth - cost; the help an hour = cost / hours. Noodle: the lines you keep (by default housing, utilities, phone and internet, groceries, getting around, insurance, health, child care, debt minimums) added up; months = cash / that. Pay yourself first: the parts added up; a paycheck = that / paychecks a month; what is left = take-home - the parts that leave it. M72 loop: from $0, s of take-home a month at the return, monthly, until (1 - s) x take-home x 12 / WR. 1b: what you own - what you owe, by group. 3: each month of the money log, money in, money out, each category / the real hourly wage = hours of life.

column2: What it is / What it could be: the standard FI number and its age, the same after what is counted, and the layer chart year by year
column3: Run A, Nov 27 2026 (js/math/paylayers.js, copied to game/core/paylayers.js; the game shows it in game/features/couldbe.js). What it is = spending a year / the withdrawal rate (25 times at 4%); its age = the first year the investments (growing each year, with the year's saving going in) reach it. What it could be = what must be invested the day work stops so that it pays each year's cost less the steady income that was counted, to 95, and then keeps paying the last year's amount for good; each year is counted back at the withdrawal rate, so with nothing counted it equals What it is. Its age = the first year the investments reach the target for that age. Things that can be counted: Social Security (a share), other steady income, a spending shape by age bands, health insurance before 65, tax on traditional withdrawals (the last two can raise it). The layer chart, for each age from today to 95: the line = needs (the FAT share of spending) + wants + health insurance of your own from the year work stops until 65 + tax on that year's traditional withdrawals. What pays, in order: Social Security and other steady income (matched to the needs first), work, then the accounts (taxable, traditional, Roth; the HSA pays health insurance first). Gap = the line less the layers. A layer that is switched off pays nothing.
